cells.tense: You are here, with the pen, and what is finished can be left finished.
cells.act: stand where the giving can be witnessed
cells.ask: Take something you did for someone quietly and do a piece of it where they can see you, with no explaining after.
cells.core:
What you look after — plants, people, the arrangements that keep a household running — you trim to what will actually hold. A thing can finish in your hands without a case being made for it. The ending is what frees the space, and you have the nerve to go through with it rather than around it.
And to keep going, let the hand show. Take something you did for someone quietly and do a piece of it where they can see you, with no explaining after. What gets seen is lighter to carry. You hold two claims at once without dropping either; that is your craft here. It is also the part you keep hidden, which is why the acknowledging you are owed has a hard time reaching you.
cells.sheetLine: You tend what grows by knowing what is finished.
cells.verb: tending what grows by giving it a form that lasts
cells.place: at the close of what has to end before anything begins

cells.tense: You are already clearing ground for a season that has not arrived.
cells.act: let the satisfaction of a finished thing land
cells.ask: Sit with one thing already finished before you improve it. Let the satisfaction land, then leave the hour alone.
cells.core:
You are pruning for a season no one can see yet. Somewhere ahead, the end has to happen, and you are already there with both hands on it — clearing before the thing has finished being alive for the others at the table. It looks like foresight and you give it that name, but forward of now the branch is still green. Care that doesn't exhaust runs on a full store, not a seized one.
Where it tips is completion: nothing you tend gets to finish in your hands. Sit with one thing already finished before you improve it. Let the satisfaction land, then leave the hour alone. The clearing after that is smaller and the right size. Reach past every finished thing and there is nothing you built left standing in — including this.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you.
cells.act: keep following the star after everything that has happened
cells.ask: Go another week on the choice you made before it got hard. No sign needed, no announcement — just carry that version forward.
cells.core:
The care that got you here was real and took years; completion is the part that went missing. The thing still matters to you, but the work on it has stopped, and you stand at its door the way you stood when it was active. What was built is finished whether or not you have said so. Patience is not the same as standing still.
So carry it differently. Go another week on the choice you made before it got hard. No sign needed, no announcement — just carry that version forward. This is the following that survives everything that has happened; it does not need the old form, only the direction. Something you raised to the end is still going somewhere. That is not a new ending. It is one already under way.

cells.tense: The hand on the tiller is yours, and it is telling itself it never took the wheel.
cells.act: accept the acknowledgment when it comes
cells.ask: Next time someone thanks you for holding something steady, take it in. Say thank you, and stop there.
cells.core:
You keep something alive for people and call it nothing. The order around you has a hand, and the hand is yours — arranging, covering, making the loose part hold. Ask you about it and you would say you just happened to be there. The ones being held up have not once believed that. They don't need to.
Let the credit land when it arrives. Next time someone thanks you for holding something steady, take it in. Say thank you, and stop there. That is where you usually turn it aside, and turning it aside is what keeps what you set down from being honored. Being thanked is the smallest shift, and it is the one that lets the cost be seen.
cells.sheetLine: You are the steady hand and the one who calls it nothing.
